description: Implement all JavaScript interactivity in js/script.js: page loader, Intersection Observer scroll-reveal animations, countdown timer targeting Feb 19 2027 11:40 PM IST, HTML Canvas scratch-card with mouse+touch support, parallax hero background, smooth scroll for anchor links, and music-toggle button state. Depends on FEAT-001 (HTML structure and CSS classes must already exist).
steps: Step 1 — Create js/script.js with an IIFE or DOMContentLoaded wrapper. All code goes inside to avoid global scope pollution. Structure the file with clearly commented sections for each feature module: // === LOADER === , // === SCROLL REVEAL === , // === COUNTDOWN === , // === SCRATCH CARD === , // === PARALLAX === , // === SMOOTH SCROLL === , // === MUSIC TOGGLE ===

Step 2 — Loader module. On DOMContentLoaded, set a timeout of ~1.5s (enough for fonts to load), then add class 'loader-hidden' to the #loader element. Listen for the transitionend event on #loader and set display:none after the fade-out completes. As a fallback, also hide it after 3s maximum even if transition doesn't fire.

Step 3 — Scroll Reveal module using Intersection Observer. Query all elements with class 'reveal'. Create an IntersectionObserver with options { threshold: 0.15, rootMargin: '0px 0px -50px 0px' }. On intersection (entry.isIntersecting), add class 'active' to the target and unobserve it (one-shot animation). This triggers the CSS transition from opacity:0/translateY(30px) to opacity:1/translateY(0). Ensure every <section> and key inner elements (.event-card, .timeline-item, .gallery-item, .couple-card, .family-card, .venue-item, .countdown-box) have the 'reveal' class in the HTML — if FEAT-001 didn't add it to all of them, add it now to the HTML file.

Step 4 — Countdown Timer module. Define the target date: new Date('2027-02-19T23:40:00+05:30') for Feb 19 2027 11:40 PM IST. Create an updateCountdown() function that calculates the difference between target and Date.now(), extracts days/hours/minutes/seconds, and updates the textContent of #countdown-days, #countdown-hours, #countdown-minutes, #countdown-seconds. When a number changes from the previous value, add a 'tick' class to the element, then remove it after 600ms (triggering the CSS scale animation @keyframes tick). Call updateCountdown() immediately, then setInterval(updateCountdown, 1000). If the target date has passed, show '0' for all values and clear the interval.

Step 5 — Scratch Card module (Canvas) — Setup. Query all three <canvas> elements inside .scratch-cards. For each canvas: set width/height attributes to match their CSS rendered size (use canvas.offsetWidth, canvas.offsetHeight, accounting for devicePixelRatio for sharp rendering). Get the 2D context. Draw the cover layer: fill with var(--color-gold) equivalent (#c9a84c), then draw a heart shape using bezier curves (ctx.beginPath, ctx.moveTo, ctx.bezierCurveTo to form a heart outline, ctx.fill). Set globalCompositeOperation = 'destination-out' for erasing on scratch. Store a scratchProgress counter per canvas.

Step 6 — Scratch Card module (Canvas) — Mouse event handlers. For each canvas, add mousedown, mousemove, mouseup event listeners. On mousedown: set isScratching = true, store canvas-relative coordinates. On mousemove (if isScratching): calculate position via (e.clientX - rect.left), erase a circle at that position using ctx.arc + ctx.fill with globalCompositeOperation = 'destination-out', radius ~20px. On mouseup: set isScratching = false, calculate scratch percentage by reading pixel data (ctx.getImageData) and counting transparent pixels — if > 50% scratched, mark that canvas as revealed. Track all 3 canvases; when all 3 are revealed, add 'visible' class to .date-reveal to show the date with the CSS transition.

Step 7 — Scratch Card module (Canvas) — Touch event handlers for mobile. Add touchstart, touchmove, touchend events to each canvas, mirroring the mouse logic. Use e.touches[0].clientX/Y for coordinates. Call e.preventDefault() on touchmove to prevent page scroll while scratching. Use { passive: false } when adding touchmove listener. The canvas elements should already have CSS touch-action: none. On touchend, calculate scratch percentage same as mouseup. Ensure the heart cover is drawn identically for touch devices.

Step 8 — Parallax module for hero background. On scroll event (throttled via requestAnimationFrame to avoid jank), read window.scrollY. If scrollY < window.innerHeight (user is still near hero), translate the hero's ::before background pseudo-element downward by scrollY * 0.3 using transform: translateY(). Apply this to the .hero element itself or a .hero-bg child div. Use a flag to ensure only one rAF is queued at a time. On mobile (<768px), reduce the parallax factor to 0.15 or disable entirely for performance.

Step 9 — Smooth Scroll module. If there are any anchor links (<a href='#section-id'>), add click event listeners that call e.preventDefault() and use element.scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth', block: 'start' }). This covers potential navigation links or any in-page anchors. Also apply scroll-behavior: smooth to the <html> element via JS as a fallback.

Step 10 — Music Toggle module. Query the .music-toggle button. On click, toggle the 'paused' class on the button (which controls the CSS animation of the bars inside). This is visual-only — no actual audio playback. Set initial state to 'paused' (bars not animating). Store state in a simple boolean variable.

Step 11 — Final polish pass on index.html. Ensure every element that should animate on scroll has the 'reveal' class. Add appropriate stagger classes (.stagger-1, .stagger-2, etc.) to: event cards (3 cards), timeline items (5 items), gallery items (4 items), venue items (4 items), countdown boxes (4 boxes), family cards (2 cards). Verify the music-toggle button HTML has 3 <span> elements inside for the animated bars. Verify each canvas has proper data attributes and a sibling label. Verify all IDs referenced by JS exist in the HTML.
acceptance_criteria: Page loader appears for ~1.5s then fades out, revealing content.
Scrolling down triggers fade-in + slide-up animations on each section and on individual cards/items within sections.
Staggered animations are visible — event cards, timeline items, and gallery items animate in sequence with slight delays.
Countdown timer displays correct Days/Hours/Minutes/Seconds until Feb 19 2027 11:40 PM IST and updates every second.
Countdown numbers have a subtle scale/fade animation (tick) when values change.
Scratch card canvases display gold heart shapes that can be scratched away with mouse drag to reveal content underneath.
Scratch card canvases work with touch events on mobile — finger drag scratches the hearts.
When all three hearts are scratched >50%, the date reveal ('Friday, 19 February 2027' / 'Phere at the muhurat of 11:40 pm') animates into view.
Hero section has a subtle parallax effect on scroll (background moves at a slower rate).
Music toggle button toggles between animated and paused bar states on click.
No JavaScript errors in the browser console.
Animations maintain 60fps — only transform and opacity are animated, no layout-triggering properties.
verification: Open /Users/mukul.gaddhyan/Git/shadhi/card1/index.html in a browser and confirm the loader appears then fades away.
Scroll through the entire page — each section and card should fade/slide in as it enters the viewport.
Verify the countdown shows the correct time remaining until Feb 19 2027 11:40 PM IST.
Click and drag on each of the three heart canvases — gold layer should erase, revealing text underneath. After all three are scratched, the full date should appear below.
On mobile or using Chrome DevTools device emulator (375px width, touch simulation): swipe/drag on scratch cards and confirm touch events work.
Check the browser console (F12 > Console) for any JavaScript errors — there should be none.
Click the music toggle button — the animated bars inside should toggle between moving and static.
Scroll back to the hero and observe the subtle parallax shift on the background.
findings: All JS interactivity implemented in js/script.js inside an IIFE. Loader fades after 1.5s with 3s fallback. IntersectionObserver triggers .active on all 35 .reveal elements (threshold 0.15, rootMargin -50px). Countdown targets new Date('2027-02-19T23:40:00+05:30') with tick animation on number change. Scratch card uses Canvas 2D with devicePixelRatio scaling, willReadFrequently hint, bezier-curve hearts filled with #c9a84c, destination-out compositing for erasing, both mouse and touch handlers (touchmove uses passive:false + preventDefault). Date reveal triggers when all 3 canvases >50% scratched. Parallax on .hero-bg-pattern throttled via rAF (0.3 factor desktop, 0.15 mobile). Music toggle starts paused, toggles .paused class on click. Smooth scroll set on html + click handler for anchor links. Added .countdown-number.tick CSS rule to apply the @keyframes tick animation. No HTML changes needed — FEAT-001 already had all required classes, IDs, data attributes, and stagger classes in place.
